I.1Preamble

\[I.1.1 corrected by [PR733627](https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/awardsandorders/html/pr733627.htm) ppc 07Sep21\]

I.1.1[Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81812477) provides for the payment of a percentage amount above an employee’s ordinary hourly rate (Loaded Rate) in satisfaction of the requirement to pay overtime, penalty rates (except public holiday penalty rates) and the split shift allowance in clause [26.14(b)(i)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479230937). In particular:

(a)[Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81812477) provides for 6 different Loaded Rate percentages (see clause [I.5.1](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820081)).

(b)Clause [I.4](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820144) sets out the Loaded Rate Parameters—that is, the pattern of hours that may be worked in respect of each of the Loaded Rate percentages.

(c)Loaded Rate Arrangements do not apply to certain categories of employees (see clause [I.3](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820122)).

(d)The creation, variation and termination of Loaded Rate Arrangements is set out in clause [I.2](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81817163).

(e)Disputes about the operation of a Loaded Rate Arrangement can be dealt with in accordance with clause [I.8](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820215).

NOTE: Loaded Rate Arrangements under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81812477) only apply to full-time adult employees classified at Level 3 and above.

I.2Loaded rate arrangement—creation and termination

I.2.1Subject to the provisions of [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81812477), an employer may elect to pay a full-time employee classified at Level 3 or above, a Loaded Rate in satisfaction of the requirements of:

(a)clause  [26.14(b)(i)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479230937)— [Split shift allowance](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref478308614);

(b)clause  [28](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref476062418)— [Overtime](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref476062418) but not clauses [28.2(d)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref32572797) to [(f)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref503425402); and

(c)clause  [29](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479238353)— [Penalty rates](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479238353), with the exception of penalty rates in relation to public holidays.

NOTE: An employee’s ordinary hourly rate is defined clause [2](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref461031031)— [Definitions](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref461031031).

I.2.2If an employer elects to pay an employee a Loaded Rate, the employer must provide the employee with a written loaded rate arrangement in accordance with the form set out in [Schedule J](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81817542) [—Loaded Rate Arrangement Form](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81817545).

I.2.3The employer must keep a copy of the Loaded Rate Arrangement and any document terminating that arrangement as a time and wages record.

I.2.4Subject to clause [39](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287630)— [Consultation about changes to rosters or hours of work](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287630), an employer may vary the Loaded Rate Arrangement by giving 2 weeks’ written notice of the issuing a new Loaded Rate Arrangement.

I.2.5A Loaded Rate Arrangement may be terminated:

(a)at any time by written agreement between the employee and the employer; or

(b)by the employer giving 2 weeks’ written notice.

I.2.6A Loaded Rate Arrangement terminated in accordance with clause [I.2.5(b)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81817697) ceases to have effect at the end of the notice period.

I.3Loaded rate arrangements not to be applied to certain employees

I.3.1 [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81812477) does not apply to part-time or casual employees or to employees:

(a)classified at the introductory level, Level 1 or Level 2;

(b)paid in accordance with clause [18.4](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref489347012)— [Junior rates](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref489347012);

(c)paid in accordance with clause [E.4](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81920940)— [Supported wage rates](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81920940);

(d)engaged in accordance with clause [15.3](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref503532150)— [Catering in remote locations](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref503532150); and

(e)rostered in accordance with clause [15.1(b)(vii)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref31991692) of this award.

I.4Loaded rate parameters

I.4.1A Loaded Rate is only in satisfaction of the payments set out at clause  [I.2.1(a)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81819180), [(b)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820321) and [(c)](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820326) if all of the following rostering requirements are met (Loaded Rate Parameters):

(a)the roster cycle must operate weekly commencing on a Monday;

(b)Monday to Friday: a maximum of 11.5 hours (excluding meal breaks) per day / shift rostered between 7:00am and 12:00am (midnight);

(c)Saturday: a maximum of 10 hours (excluding meal breaks);

(d)Sunday: a maximum of 10 hours (excluding meal breaks); and

(e)if the period between shifts is 3 hours or less, a split shift allowance must be paid.

I.5.5The Loaded Rate Percentage will only apply to, and be in satisfaction of, work performed and the allowances specified within the Loaded Rate Parameters.

NOTE 1: An employee will be entitled to overtime in accordance with clause [28](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref476062418)— [Overtime](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref476062418) for work which exceeds the daily and/or shift maximum hours, the Loaded Rate Range of Days or the Loaded Rate Maximum Weekly Hours each week.

NOTE 2: Under the [NES](https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/awards/resources/nes.pdf) (see section 62 of the [Act](http://www.legislation.gov.au/Series/C2009A00028)) an employee may refuse to work additional hours if they are unreasonable. Section 62 sets out factors to be taken into account in determining whether the additional hours are reasonable or unreasonable.

NOTE 3: An employee will be entitled to the relevant penalty rates and applicable entitlements for work completed on, or other arrangements relating to a public holiday in accordance with clause [29](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479238353)— [Penalty rates](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref479238353) and clause [35](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81920994)— [Public holidays](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81921001).

NOTE 4: If an employee performs work beyond the scope of the Loaded Rates Parameters but does not exceed the daily and/or shift maximum hours, the Loaded Rate Range of Days or the Loaded Rate Maximum Weekly Hours each week, the employee will be entitled to the applicable penalty rate or allowance in accordance with this award.

I.5.6The employer must keep a record of the starting and finishing times of work, and any unpaid breaks taken. This record must be signed by the employee or acknowledged as correct in writing (including by electronic means) by the employee, each pay period or roster cycle.

I.6Base rate of pay for employees on a loaded rate arrangement

For the purposes of the [NES](https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/awards/resources/nes.pdf), the base rate of pay of an employee receiving a Loaded Rate under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820612) is the employee’s ordinary hourly rate and excludes any incentive-based payments, bonuses, loadings, monetary allowances, overtime and penalties.

I.7Consultation

At least 7 days prior to initiating any of the provisions in [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820621), the employer must consult with all employees affected by the proposed change and their representatives (if any).

I.8Dispute settlement—consent arbitration

I.8.1Any dispute regarding the operation of [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820629) may be referred to the Fair Work Commission in accordance with clause [40](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287505)— [Dispute resolution](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287505).

I.8.2An employer who enters into a Loaded Rate Arrangement under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820665) provides consent to a dispute arising from the arrangement being settled by the Fair Work Commission through arbitration in accordance with clause [40](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287505)— [Dispute resolution](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref494287505) and section 739(4) of the [Act](http://www.legislation.gov.au/Series/C2009A00028).

I.8.3In arbitrating a dispute the Fair Work Commission may:

(a)terminate an agreement made under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820709) if it determines that the employer failed to consult as required by clause [I.7](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820720);

(b)require an employer to pay an employee the difference between what they were paid under the Loaded Rate Arrangement and what they would otherwise have received under this Award if the Fair Work Commission determines that the arrangement entered into under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820709) was unfair to the employee; and

(c)terminate a Loaded Rate Arrangement if the Fair Work Commission determines that the arrangement entered into under [Schedule I](https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000009.html#_Ref81820709) is unfair to the employee.
